bug_semantics: The authenticated ticket routes trusted a user-controlled numeric ticket id without constraining the selected Ticket to Auth::user()->company_id. GET /ticket/update/{id} returned another tenant's ticket data and, after attachment support was added, enumerated that ticket's attachment directory; POST /ticket/save accepted an id, loaded that arbitrary Ticket, overwrote its fields and company_id, and thereby let the caller hijack it; GET /ticket/delete/{id} loaded and deleted an arbitrary Ticket while using generic Request, so neither tenant ownership nor TicketDeleteRequest permission authorization was enforced.
flaw_origin: The core cross-tenant read and write/hijack mechanism originated in the initial ticket CRUD commit 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd: TicketUpdateController called Ticket::find($id), and TicketSaveController called Ticket::find($request->id) before assigning the authenticated user's company_id, with no ownership predicate. Commit 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 later extended the same trust error to deletion, commit 626b0228c248637086ce91bb17b2ec1b1c21961b later extended the read impact to attachments, and repository/refactor changes preserved rather than originated the core flaw.
ai_marker: absent — the raw commit object for 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd names Gustavo Novaro <gnovaro@gmail.com> as both author and committer and contains only the subject "Tickets CRUD"; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The supplied GHSA names b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9 as its fix. git show of that commit changes TicketUpdateController and TicketRepository from Ticket::find(...) to id-plus-company_id queries ending in firstOrFail(), and changes TicketDeleteController from generic Illuminate\Http\Request and Ticket::find($id) to TicketDeleteRequest plus the same company_id constraint. The commit also adds the ticket permissions and cross-tenant security tests.

git log -L on TicketUpdateController::update traced the unscoped Ticket::find($id) through later formatting, attachment, and migration changes to file creation in 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd. git log -L on the pre-repository TicketSaveController::save likewise traced Ticket::find($request->id) and the subsequent company_id assignment to that same commit; 65f6b9f961efe533b4d3f20f1eddad132fe8ef1d merely moved this behavior into TicketRepository.

git show 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd shows the newly added /ticket/update/{id} and /ticket/save routes and newly added controllers containing the two vulnerable lookups. git cat-file -p records its sole parent as 063d713c71ca6c453d43e7b17a9ee2f8b2fc0ce1. git ls-tree -r of that immediate parent shows neither app/Http/Controllers/Ticket nor resources/views/ticket, and the commit's routes/web.php diff adds the ticket routes from absence; therefore the vulnerable reachable read/write mechanism is absent from the immediate parent tree.

git show 946a0c5e43a1178534e5b013ea2608d565686220 shows the later addition of GET /ticket/delete/{id} and TicketDeleteController::delete using Ticket::find($id)->delete() with generic Request and no ownership or permission check. git show c837c80a4f7de40348e142af7d15e60c39ebcaf1 shows TicketDeleteRequest was created in 2026 with authorize() checking 'delete ticket' but was not wired into the controller; the direct fix finally wired it. These later commits explain the deletion lifecycle but are not the earliest BIC for the advisory's already-existing cross-tenant ticket flaw.

git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd is an ancestor of b2b6ffdace0972ab62d1f7e8cdab0ed213bfc4a9. git tag --contains the BIC includes v1.0.0, v2.0.1, v4.6.0, v5.5.3, and v5.14.0, establishing that the flaw predates the affected released line. The fix's parent 361566c1ddb01df16f2cff0aa836f04be174f3c4 bumps APP_VERSION to 5.4.8; descendant 7e86b0845b14887b101a4516020fedafbff23564 changes 5.4.8 to 5.4.9 specifically 'after ticket security fixes'. git tag --contains the fix returns v5.5.3 and v5.14.0, and the referenced GitHub v5.5.3 release is titled 'Big security upgrade', so the fix is present at the advisory's 5.4.9 internal patched boundary and in the first referenced public security release.

git cat-file -p 2feef9f35593dba39525f6a8a07b4cd3f74f19bd is the only AI-attribution evidence considered: it has human author/committer identity and no trailers. The Claude co-author trailers on later security-hardening and fix/version-bump commits are outside the BIC commit object and therefore do not attribute the introduction under the protocol.
reasoning: The smallest causal origin is not the 2023 repository extraction, the 2024 Laravel migration, or the 2026 AI-assisted fix: line history crosses those mechanical changes and reaches the initial 2022 Tickets CRUD commit. That commit made attacker-selected ids reachable and first wrote both unscoped read and unscoped update lookups; the save path's forced reassignment to the current company turns an arbitrary cross-tenant update into tenant hijacking. Its immediate parent lacks the ticket controllers, views, and routes, directly proving absence. Deletion and attachment disclosure were later expansions of the same object-ownership failure and are included in the lifecycle without replacing the earliest real BIC. The direct fix scopes all three selections to the authenticated company and activates delete permission authorization; the immediate 5.4.9 version bump and containing v5.5.3 release establish the patched boundary. Because the BIC's raw commit object has no AI marker and identifies a human author and committer, the BIC-only verdict is NOT_AI despite AI attribution on later non-BIC commits.
